newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian court sentences five militants to death.
newsitem.headline: Algerian court sentences five militants to death.

text.p: An Algerian court on Monday sentenced a Moslem militant to 20 years in prison and five others in absentia to death for killing an Italian businessman, the official Algerian news agency APS said.
The six were convicted of involvement in the killing of Italian businessman Angelo Gavisoli late in 1995 inside sock plant near Oran, APS said.
More than 1,000 Moslem militants have been sentenced to death, mostly in absentia, since 1993 when Algerian courts began trials of people for fundamentalist activism.

About 60,000 people, including more than 100 foreigners, have died in Algeria's violence since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
